Sam Altman (born April 22, 1985) is an American entrepreneur and investor best known as the CEO of OpenAI, the AI research lab behind ChatGPT, which he co-founded in 2015. A prominent figure in Silicon Valley, he previously served as president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator (2014–2019) and is considered a key, often controversial, leader in the development of artificial general intelligence (AGI). This video discusses Sam Altman's, the CEO of OpenAI, perspective on building the future of AI:1ma16zYouTube• Oct 8, 2025 1m Key Details About Sam Altman: Role at OpenAI: As CEO, Altman has steered OpenAI from a nonprofit research lab to a commercial powerhouse, raising billions and forming a close partnership with Microsoft. He was briefly fired and rehired by the board in November 2023. Background: Born in Chicago and raised in St. Louis, Altman studied computer science at Stanford University before dropping out to co-found the location-based social networking app Loopt, which was part of Y Combinator's first batch in 2005. Y Combinator Era: He became president of Y Combinator in 2014, succeeding founder Paul Graham, and is credited with expanding the accelerator's focus to include more ambitious, hard-tech startups. Vision & Impact: Known for his focus on long-term, high-impact technologies, Altman is a major investor in energy and tech companies, including Stripe and Helion Energy. Personal Life: Altman is gay and has spoken about how finding online communities during his youth in the Midwest was transformative. Controversies & Safety: He frequently testifies before Congress on AI regulation, arguing for the need to manage existential risks, though he has faced scrutiny over safety practices and the rapid pace of OpenAI's development. Recent Events: As of April 2026, he has been in the news due to security incidents at his San Francisco home. Altman's career has been characterized by high-stakes risk-taking and a belief that AI, specifically AGI, will fundamentally change human civilization.
